text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is usually a "silent killer" because it rarely causes any noticeable warning signs. Most people can live with high blood pressure for years without feeling anything unusual.
snippet_highlighted_words: rarely causes any noticeable warning signs

text_blocks.snippet: Symptoms usually only show up if your blood pressure spikes to dangerously high levels (a hypertensive crisis, typically 180/120 mm Hg or higher).
Signs of a severe spike or hypertensive emergency can include:

list.snippet: Severe headaches or pressure in the head
Shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
Blurty vision or other vision changes
Nosebleeds or blood spots in the eyes

text_blocks.snippet: Because you cannot rely on how you feel, regular checks are essential. You can learn more about blood pressure ranges through the American Heart Association or read the detailed overview on Mayo Clinic.

list.snippet: Stage 2 Hypertension: 140/90 mm Hg or higher
Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180/120 mm Hg (Seek emergency medical help immediately if paired with symptoms like chest pain or shortness of breath)
